text: Proposition two changes how California saves for bad
budget years.
Current rules stop requiring additional deposits when that
account reaches ten percent of General Fund tax
revenues.
Proposition two raises that threshold to twenty percent
and requires more saving in particularly strong
investment-tax years.
It changes the rules over time;
it does not instantly double the money already
saved.
The measure also extends required extra debt payments
from twenty thirty through twenty forty, and expands
the debts those payments can address.
A voter might prefer a stronger buffer against
service cuts,
emergency borrowing, or tax increases during a downturn.
Another voter could prioritize services or infrastructure
now.
Yes changes reserve and extra-debt-payment rules;
no keeps the current rules.
